summary: MIT researchers developed methods to enforce physics-based constraints within AI models for predicting chaotic systems, preventing physically impossible predictions in weather, climate, and turbulent flows. Published November 20 in PNAS, the approach enables data-driven models for complex nonlinear
takeaways: Method enforces energy dissipation as hard constraint on predictions
Prevents drift into physically impossible weather and climate forecasts
Applies to weather, climate, aviation turbulence, ocean currents

summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Neon, described as frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion for complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows. The model is production-ready for code generation, enterprise and analytical work, scientific applications, and cyber
takeaways: Frontier-level intelligence for software engineering and science workflows
Production-ready for code generation and enterprise applications
Production-ready for code, enterprise, analytical, scientific, and cyber defense applications

title: Linguistic Style Emerges as Attack Surface for LLM Safety
summary: Researchers from multiple institutions demonstrated that linguistic style functions as a previously overlooked attack surface for large language model safety mechanisms. title: Verifiable Logic in Medical LLMs: Neuro-Symbolic Grounding for Clinical Reasoning
summary: A critical review identifies how clinical large language models produce fluent outputs through invalid reasoning that static benchmarks miss, examining confident hallucination, causally invalid inference, and spurious shortcuts. The paper proposes neuro-symbolic grounding using formal logic engines
takeaways: Three failure modes: confident hallucination, causally invalid inference, spurious shortcuts
Proposes neuro-symbolic grounding using logic engines and knowledge graphs
Current regulation inadequate; calls for auditing reasoning trajectories alongside accuracy

title: Structured Analysis of Chain-of-Thought Failure Modes in LLM Reasoning
summary: Researchers introduced CoT2Graph, a framework that represents chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning traces as directed dependency graphs to analyze failure modes in large language model reasoning. The method makes relationships between reasoning steps explicit and captures structural patterns including b

title: EconSafeBench Measures Safety of LLM Agents Under Economic Pressures
summary: Researchers Yuzhu Ling, Jiale Han, and Benyou Wang introduced EconSafeBench, the first benchmark for evaluating the safety of large language model agents making consequential economic decisions in executable economic environments. The benchmark contains 828 cases across five economic scenarios and f

title: Self-Evolving Dual-Role Model for Medication Recommendation from EHRs
summary: SEMPA is a training-free agentic framework for medication recommendation from electronic health records that couples a Proposer agent with a Critic agent in multi-round adversarial deliberation. The system grounds medication candidates with molecular-aware retrieval, contrastively evolves both agent

title: Medical LLM Judges Show Self-Preference Bias in Clinical Content Evaluation
summary: Analysis reveals that LLMs used as judges for medical content evaluation favor outputs from the same model family, creating circular bias independent of clinical quality.

title: LLMs Exhibit Hallucination and Overconfidence When Answering Underspecified Questions
summary: Study shows large language models readily answer incomplete questions with high confidence, with query underspecification driving hallucination rather than model limitations alone.

title: Paper reveals privacy risks in AI agentic skills and plugins
summary: A new research paper identifies how agent skills—installable instructions for AI assistants—may expose or infer sensitive user information even when functioning correctly.

title: Medical agents using recursive self-improvement and clinical co-evolution framework
summary: A new framework enables medical LLM agents to recursively improve from their own experience rather than remaining static, reducing recurring errors across patient cases.

title: Paper reveals language models memorize their own hallucinations during post-training
summary: Research shows that applying reasoning-centric post-training recipes across domains causes language models to memorize and reinforce their own hallucinated outputs.

title: Observation Bias in Clinical AI Evaluation
summary: Clinical AI systems face systematic bias from incomplete medical documentation that captures only clinician-noticed findings, skewing evaluation and downstream publications.

title: HiSA: Sparsifying the Hidden Dimension of RoPE Attention in LLMs
summary: Hidden Sparse Attention reduces computational cost of attention in large language models by sparsifying dot product computation without sacrificing effectiveness.

title: UK Tech Leaders Adopting AI Faster Than Governance Frameworks
summary: British technology leaders are implementing AI systems at a faster pace than establishing related regulatory and governance structures.

title: Data Centers' Electricity Consumption Damages Air Quality Far Beyond Their Locations
summary: Research reveals that air pollution from data center electricity use extends across long distances, with significant impacts in the Midwest.

title: Quantum computing enables previously impossible competitive game
summary: A game has been created that cannot be won without a quantum computer, demonstrating a computational advantage of quantum systems.

title: MIT Advances AI Text Detector Robustness Against Evolving Models
summary: MIT researchers developed a more flexible training method to make AI-generated text detectors resilient when new models emerge or text is disguised as human-written.

title: RAW measures user cost of refusals in deployed language models
summary: A new causal measurement method (RAW) quantifies how often deployed LLM users disengage after request refusals, filling a blind spot in production model monitoring.

title: Sycophancy in LLMs: Distinguishing Genuine Agreement from Inappropriate Deference
summary: Researchers study sycophancy in large language models by separating appropriate agreement from inappropriate agreement-seeking behavior.

title: Financial Sentiment Analysis Models Vulnerable to Adversarial Text Modifications
summary: Despite high benchmark accuracy, financial sentiment analysis models like FinBERT remain vulnerable to subtle adversarial text modifications, raising risks for automated trading and portfolio management.

title: SAFE-Triage: Multidimensional Evaluation Framework for Patient-Facing Emergency Triage AI
summary: SAFE-Triage framework evaluates patient-facing emergency triage AI beyond acuity accuracy using human review, automated metrics, and LLM-as-judge evaluation.

title: EGS: Complementary Safety Framework for Educational LLMs
summary: EGS framework extends educational LLM safety beyond benign compliance to prevent toxic, biased, misleading, or developmentally inappropriate content for adolescent users.

title: NSF invests $90 million in three new Science and Technology Centers
summary: The National Science Foundation awarded $90 million in funding to establish three new Science and Technology Centers supporting transformative research.

title: Study profiles hallucinations in frontier LLMs for medical entity linking
summary: Research evaluates how much frontier LLMs hallucinate when linking clinical entities to medical ontologies, revealing reliability concerns for healthcare.

title: Fact-Checking LLMs Show Degraded Performance on Multilingual and Noisy Evidence
summary: Study evaluates robustness of large language models at automated fact-checking when evidence is incomplete, misleading, or in low-resource languages.

title: Clinical Language Models Vulnerable to Temporal Leakage in Discharge Prediction
summary: Hospital discharge prediction models rely on explicit discharge-related lexical cues in clinical notes even when temporally filtered, raising validity concerns for clinical use.

title: Decision 1.0: Open-Weight Foundation Model for Reusable Judgments in Software
summary: Open-weight model family designed to encapsulate reusable decision-making components (action selection, condition testing, evidence assessment) for integration into software control flow.

title: Research shows reinforcement learning can recover from severely corrupted training data in reasoning tasks
summary: A study demonstrates that reinforcement learning can enable language models to perform well on mathematical reasoning even when supervised fine-tuning data is heavily corrupted.

title: Research demonstrates weight-space programming enables in-context learning without gradient descent
summary: A study shows that language models can read and rewrite another network's weights using only examples, achieving performance comparable to fine-tuning.

title: Paper proposes comprehensive evaluation framework for child safety in large language models
summary: Researchers present an evaluation framework for child safety in language models that moves beyond prompt-based heuristics to assess broader safety alignment.

title: Research identifies cross-platform production signatures of state-linked information operations
summary: A study shows that information operations active across multiple platforms exhibit consistent production signatures in timing and account behavior despite varying identities and content.

title: LongCat Recall: Sparse Attention Optimization for Extended Context Retrieval
summary: A new sparse attention method co-designs key organization and retrieval to reduce computational overhead in long-context inference tasks.

title: Phantom Context Influence: Hidden Word Steering in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
summary: Language models disproportionately rely on specific context words to drive chain-of-thought reasoning, independent of their semantic relevance.

title: DTS: Delta-Based Tile Scoring for Long-Context Sparse Attention in LLMs
summary: DTS enables efficient long-context attention in large language models by intelligently scoring which blocks of the attention matrix to skip during prefill.

title: Differentially private LLM inference via dummy-augmented shuffling
summary: New privacy technique enables secure LLM-as-a-Service inference by protecting sensitive user queries from exposure.

title: HireWatch: Evaluating LLM Compliance With U.S. Employment Law Under Contextual Pressure
summary: HireWatch is an evaluation framework assessing whether large language models comply with U.S. employment law when deployed in hiring.

title: Monitoring Medical LLMs Through Verbalized Internal States
summary: Internal model states rendered in natural language can reveal what medical LLMs know but do not explicitly state, improving safety monitoring.

title: RoCoKV: KV Cache Compression for Long-Reasoning LLM Inference
summary: Uncertainty and redundancy-aware KV cache compression accelerates inference for reasoning models by removing redundant tokens from long traces.

title: PAIR-MED: Policy-Reward Alternation for Multilingual Medical Reasoning
summary: Iterative refinement using process reward models improves medical question-answering across languages despite fixed reward model limitations.

title: MATE: Trustworthy Execution Layer for Mobile Agents
summary: MATE controls the boundary between agent proposals and actual execution on personal smartphones, protecting sensitive data and payments.

title: STARK: Personalized Agents with Long-Term Learning and Memory
summary: Architecture improvements enable agents to learn and remember user interactions over extended periods, capturing both what happened and why.

title: Auditing Human-in-the-Loop CV Sorter for Academic Hiring
summary: A deployed curriculum vitae priority sorter at an academic job platform shows how to verify and audit human-in-the-loop AI systems in hiring.

title: Transformer Models of Criminal Court Case Proceedings
summary: Transformer models are developed to map complex criminal legal processes from arraignment through resolution, addressing decision-making at each stage.

title: LLM Hallucinations in Academic Authorship Attribution
summary: Large language models hallucinate fictional authors when prompted for academic authorship, with prevalence of factual information in training data playing a key role.

title: Language Models Overstate Research Novelty and Related Work Coverage
summary: Large language models make open research questions sound partly studied and overstate what related papers establish when validating research questions.

title: Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning and Out-of-Context Hallucination
summary: Analysis of the relationship between in-context learning capabilities and out-of-context hallucinations in large language models reveals mechanistic insights.

title: Gender Stereotyping in LLM-Generated Children's Stories
summary: Analysis shows large language models embed gender stereotypes in children's stories, raising concerns about narrative portrayals for young audiences.

title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview: Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Language Model
summary: OVHcloud releases Clover, a 35-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 3B activated parameters and thinking-mode generation.

title: MIT-led team uses AI to analyze code sharing across nearly 4,000 medical studies
summary: Researchers from MIT and Dana-Farber Institute used large language models to examine code sharing and information gaps in nearly 4,000 medical studies.

title: CrisisBench evaluates LLM performance on crisis counseling tasks
summary: CrisisBench is a new evaluation suite that assesses how well large language models handle crisis counseling duties including risk assessment and de-escalation.

title: LLM Agent Confidence Signals: Separating Answer Ranking, Abstention, and Error Recovery
summary: A study shows that confidence signals in LLM agents cannot be assumed to simultaneously discriminate answer quality, justify abstention, and enable recovery—each requires independent validation.

title: Attention Head Specialization: Phase Transitions in Sample Complexity
summary: New research reveals how attention heads specialize into distinct functions during neural network training with sharp phase transitions in learning efficiency.

title: SKILL.PNG: Learning Agent Skills in Pixel Space
summary: New approach enables AI agents to learn continuously optimizable skills directly from pixel observations rather than discrete textual instructions.

title: From Benchmarks to the Bench: Preference, Correspondence and Selectivity in Bidirectional Drug-Target Screening
summary: New framework improves drug-target interaction prediction by accounting for preference and selectivity in bidirectional screening for drug discovery and repurposing.

title: Sequential Anytime Valid Tests for Efficient Inference-Time Alignment
summary: Method using sequential statistical tests reduces computational waste in inference-time alignment by applying flexible budgets per prompt instead of fixed allocations.

title: PosteriorBench: Evaluating Behavior Posterior Sampling in Language Models
summary: PosteriorBench introduces a framework for studying rare language model behaviors through posterior sampling methods rather than ordinary sampling.

title: Goal-Guided Reinforcement Learning via Vision-Language Model Fine-Tuning
summary: This work uses fine-tuned vision-language models to guide exploration in reinforcement learning agents for long-horizon tasks with sparse rewards.

title: Interpretable Prototype-Conditioned Adaptation for Weather Forecasting
summary: A method using interpretable prototypes enables neural networks to learn and distinguish local weather patterns for improved forecasting.

title: LIFT: Latent Flow Matching for Probabilistic Cell Fate Dynamics
summary: LIFT uses flow matching on latent representations to model conditional cell fate outcomes from single-cell snapshot data without unique source-descendant pairings.
